front: FOB shipping point vs. FOB destination — who owns goods in transit?

back: The **consignor** (the shipper), not the consignee holding them.
Purchase price (net of discounts), **freight-in**, duties, handling to make goods saleable. **Freight-out** is a selling expense.
FIFO → lower COGS, higher income & ending inventory. LIFO → higher COGS, lower income & taxes.

front: Periodic vs. perpetual — which methods differ?
back: FIFO: **same**. LIFO and average: can **differ** (perpetual applies at each sale; moving vs. weighted average).
1) Ending ÷ current index = base-year dollars. 2) Compare to prior base total → layer. 3) Price each layer at the index **of the year it was added**; decreases come out of the newest layers.
Use LIFO for tax → must use LIFO for **financial reporting**. (IFRS bans LIFO.)
